title.narrative: Banana Pasta: Enabling better nutrition food choices in Uganda

description.narrative: Green bananas are a high-energy, high-nutrient food that grows well in many regions of Uganda and other countries in (sub-)tropical climates. However, due to a lack of appropriate post-harvest handling and storage options, the crop harvest often goes partially unused during high harvest periods. At the same time, the widespread use of middle-men and other intermediaries in green banana supply chain means that farmers get the lowest percentage of total value per kilo. The same is true of a variety of other traditional Ugandan crops like amaranth, pulses/beans and vegetables, which grow well but because of low prices and inability of storage, lack of food technology options, their potential to provide valuable & lasting nutrition is lost.The Green Banana project is about developing high nutrient pasta for the Ugandan and regional markets. Through a processing technique developed by Green Banana Food B.V., the aim is to take underutilised high nutrient food crop and using the proprietary technique to produce high quality foods for the local market. To prepare for future investments in a food processing facility for pasta production, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support for a technical feasibility study. This included prototype development, supply chain assessment, product sampling and milling process testing in order to come to a bankable business plan for further investments. The study results have been successful and further investments in a processing facility are currently being prepared. This facility may lead to a wider availability of nutritional pasta made out of banana and other crops that in turn will reduce post-harvest losses and create added value for farmers involved.
